stem: The data presented on this graph illustrate an economic effect of —

options.label: A
options.text: the rapid demobilization of U.S. defense industries after World War II

options.label: B
options.text: the federal domestic programs created as part of the Great Society

options.label: C
options.text: incentives offered under the Bracero Program to temporary laborers

options.label: D
options.text: assistance offered by the GI Bill to soldiers returning from World War II

visual_elements: Line graph titled 'New Housing Units Started, Private Ownership, 1945-1962' with x-axis labeled 'Year' from 1945 to 1962 and y-axis labeled 'Number of Units (millions)' from 0 to 2.5. Data shows an increase in housing units started peaking around 1950, then fluctuating but generally stable around 1.4 to 1.6 million.
